title: Bolstering Underutilized Industry by Leveraging Technology Transfer (BUILTT) pilot program
description: Notice of Opportunity: BUILTT for DOE Pilot Technologies The Department of Energy (DOE), in partnership with the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA), announces the availability of technologies under the Bolstering Underutilized Industry by Leveraging Technology Transfer (BUILTT) pilot program. The pilot is being conducted by the Nevada National Security Sites (NNSS), Y-12 National Security Complex, and Kansas City National Security Campus (KCNSC). Program Overview BUILTT is intended to help qualified small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) manufacture low-volume, high-impact technologies developed by DOE/NNSA Labs, Plants, and Sites. These technologies support mission requirements but may have limited commercial markets or insufficient production volume for traditional technology licensing. The program uses a Cost Reduction License (CRL), under which a qualified SMB may receive rights to produce a specified technology for a nominal licensing fee. The CRL is intended to support the sale of the resulting products to DOE, NNSA, and other government customers at a fair and reasonable pre-negotiated price. Where applicable, the CRL may also address commercial sales. Technology Areas The pilot technologies generally involve specialized manufacturing, instrumentation, sensing, materials, electronics, and analytical or production systems. Examples of technology types include: - Specialized optical and high-speed imaging equipment for experimental diagnostics; - Radiation, chemical, pressure, and environmental sensing systems; - Precision electrical and mechanical components; - Advanced materials, coatings, bonding, and fabrication processes; - Laboratory-scale mixing, processing, and production equipment; and - Software, data-analysis, and instrumentation-support technologies. A separate attachment to this posting provides the exact technology descriptions, applicable intellectual-property information, and available patent links. Prospective respondents should review that attachment to identify technologies that align with their capabilities. Eligibility and Participation Participation is open to U.S.-based SMBs that meet applicable U.S. Small Business Administration requirements. Preference may be given, when appropriate, to businesses located near participating DOE/NNSA sites and to businesses with designations such as SBA 8(a) or HUBZone. Interested businesses may be evaluated based on: - Technical and manufacturing capabilities; - Relevant facilities, equipment, personnel, and experience; - Ability to meet applicable quality, safety, security, and regulatory requirements; - Ability to support low-volume production and government customers; - Financial and organizational capacity; and - Alignment with one or more of the listed technologies. Selected respondents will be subject to vetting and due diligence before any matchmaking, licensing, or procurement activity occurs. Participation in this posting does not guarantee selection, a license, a purchase order, or a contract. How to Respond Interested businesses should contact the DOE/NNSA BUILTT program team at TPIP@nv.doe.gov with the subject line �BUILTT for DOE Pilot Technologies.� Responses should identify the respondent�s areas of interest and briefly describe relevant technical, manufacturing, and government-contracting capabilities. Additional information may be requested during the evaluation process. General Conditions Submission of a response does not create an express or implied contract between the respondent and Mission Support and Test Services, LLC (MSTS), DOE, NNSA, NNSS, Y-12, or KCNSC. MSTS and the participating organizations are not obligated to review or evaluate any response, select a respondent, issue a CRL, place an order, or award a contract. Respondents are not entitled to compensation, damages, or remuneration if this posting is modified, suspended, canceled, or not followed. title: Program Officer - Personal Services Contractor
description: U.S. DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY OFFICE OF TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM OFFICERS The U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Technical Assistance (OTA) provides technical assistance to developing and transitional countries in five functional areas: banking and financial services, budget and financial accountability, economic crimes, government debt and infrastructure finance, and revenue administration. OTA is seeking detail-oriented administrative and program support staff to serve as Program Officers for its Washington, DC-based technical assistance program. The individuals selected will be hired under personal services contracts. OTA carries out its technical assistance projects in developing and transitional countries through both resident and intermittent advisors in over 50 countries. The Program Officer is a headquarters staff position that supports OTA�s broad range of international technical assistance projects. SCOPE OF POSITION Program Officers provide administrative support and logistical assistance for multiple overseas projects in one of the five functional areas. The Program Officer assists in the deployment of expert advisors who implement the overseas projects. This includes maintaining advisor contracts; arranging travel and other logistical needs of advisors; and communicating with advisors in the field, U.S. embassies and other U.S. government partners on a regular basis. For each assigned project, the Program Officer is responsible for formulating and drafting annual project proposals and budgets and monitoring project contracts and expenditures. The Program Officer is also responsible for supporting and monitoring project activities; maintaining the historical record of all projects; preparing briefings and reports on assigned projects for internal and external distribution; and planning conferences and meetings. This position supports the operations of OTA headquarters in Washington, DC. Based on instruction from the COR, and within OTA policy, the Contractor will work at OTA office space, the Contractor�s facility, and/or travel for temporary duty domestically or internationally. QUALIFICATIONS The ideal candidate will have an undergraduate degree in public administration, international affairs, or other relevant subject matter; two to five years of work experience, preferably in project coordination, event or logistics management, or administration of U.S. government foreign assistance, NGO operations, international development, or governmental budgeting and financial management. Required Skills and Experience: Excellent written and oral communication skills. Demonstrated problem-solving and analytical skills. Strong computer skills including word processing and spreadsheet development, as well as some experience with information sharing technology such as SharePoint and video conferencing. Interpersonal skills in collaborating as part of a team. The ability to work effectively under the pressure of tight timeframes and deadlines. In addition, the following experience/knowledge is not required but is preferred: Master�s degree in public administration, international affairs, or other relevant subject matter Experience drafting project proposals, formulating budgets, and tracking expenditures. International experience in the public, private, or non-profit sectors, particularly in developing/emerging markets. Experience working with financial management information systems. Familiarity with financial management and economic concepts Foreign language ability is a plus. Please note: These are PERSONAL SERVICES CONTRACTOR positions; NOT civil service positions. U.S. citizenship is required. SALARY: The position is equivalent to a GS 9/11/12 ladder. In accordance with program regulations and based on demonstrated salary history, the current hourly rate is from $33.84 to $63.80 per hour. Background checks and Security Clearance: Secret Candidates will need to be eligible to obtain and maintain appropriate level of security clearance. Successful applicants must be able to obtain State Department medical clearance for worldwide travel. HOW TO APPLY: Applicants (individuals) should submit a cover letter and resume by e-mail to: recruitment@ota.treas.gov. Companies should not submit resumes on behalf of individuals. For consideration, emailed applications should not be sent, or contain a cc, to any OTA, IRS, or other government personnel or email address(es). Please reference Solicitation 2099AB27R00001 on your cover letter and resume. When e-mailing, the subject line must contain the following: �Solicitation 2099AB27R00001 � Program Officer � Applicant�s Last Name, First Name.� Emails received not containing this subject line will be deemed non-responsive and will not be forwarded to the program office/selection official(s) for consideration. No phone calls please and no hand carries. This announcement is open and continuous until March 31, 2027, although selections may be made in advance of that date. Please be advised that all contractors, if hired, must obtain a Unique Entity Identifier and must maintain SAM registration. The U.S. Government is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

description: Notice of Opportunity: Bolstering Underutilized Industry by Leveraging Technology Transfer (BUILTT) for DOE The Department of Energy (DOE), in partnership with the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA), announces an opportunity for small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) to participate in the Bolstering Underutilized Industry by Leveraging Technology Transfer (BUILTT) program. This pilot initiative is being conducted by the Nevada National Security Sites (NNSS), Y-12 National Security Complex, and Kansas City National Security Campus. https://www.energy.gov/technologycommercialization/fiscal-year-2025-climr-projects-commercializing-energy-technologies Program Overview: The BUILTT program is designed to facilitate the transfer of low-volume, high-impact technologies developed at DOE/NNSA Labs, Plants, and Sites (LPS) to qualified SMBs. These technologies are often mission-critical but have limited commercial markets, with the government frequently being the primary or sole customer. The program introduces a new technology transfer mechanism, the Cost Reduction License (CRL), which enables SMBs to manufacture and supply these technologies to DOE and other government agencies at a fair and reasonable price. Key Program Elements: � Technologies included in the program are anticipated to be fully developed, tested, and ready for production, but are typically excluded from traditional technology transfer due to their limited market size. � The CRL is a licensing agreement that allows SMBs to produce and sell specified technologies to DOE/NNSA at a set price, with the potential for additional commercial sales if applicable. � As applicable, the program will pool eligible technologies from participating DOE/NNSA sites and match them with vetted SMBs through a standardized process. � Depending upon SMB location, the pilot project cost share partners, including regional economic development organizations and technical service providers, may be available to assist SMBs interested in participating in BUILTT pilot. Eligibility and Participation: � Participation is open to U.S.-based small and medium-sized businesses as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration. � Preference may be given to businesses located in the regions of the participating DOE/NNSA sites and to those meeting designations such as SBA 8(a) or HUBZone. � Interested SMBs will undergo a vetting and due diligence process to assess technical capabilities and alignment with the needs of the technologies being offered. Process and Timeline: � The program will be conducted in phases, including technology identification and pooling, SMB sourcing and vetting, matchmaking, and pilot CRL execution. � Educational materials can be provided to participating SMBs regarding the licensing process and technology requirements. Additional Information: � The BUILTT program is funded by the DOE Office of Technology Commercialization and National Nuclear Security Administration and is intended to serve as a model for scalable, replicable technology transfer across DOE and other government agencies. How to Respond: Interested parties should contact the DOE/NNSA BUILTT program team at TPIP@nv.doe.gov with the subject line: �BUILTT for DOE Pilot�. TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: ThermaSpin High-Temperature Viscometer
description: Value Proposition: ThermaSpin, developed by scientists at Los Alamos National Laboratory, provides a reliable, cost-effective way to measure the flow behavior (viscosity) of extremely hot and reactive liquids, such as molten salts and metals, under realistic operating conditions. Unlike existing solutions that are expensive, complex or poorly suited for low-viscosity fluids, this enclosed high-temperature viscometer delivers high sensitivity, small sample requirements and precise atmospheric control, enabling accurate measurements without exposing materials to air or contamination. This capability is critical for industries such as advanced nuclear energy, thermal energy storage and high-temperature materials processing, where fluid properties directly impact system performance, safety and design. By making these measurements more accessible and practical, the ThermaSpin High-Temperature Viscometer reduces development risk, lowers testing costs and accelerates innovation in next-generation energy and industrial systems. The Challenge: Accurately measuring the viscosity of molten salts and other high-temperature liquids is extremely difficult because these materials exist under harsh conditions�temperatures approaching 1,000�C, high chemical reactivity and sensitivity to air and moisture. Traditional measurement techniques often lack the sensitivity needed for these low-viscosity fluids or require specialized, resource-intensive methods that are not widely accessible. In addition, many approaches demand large sample volumes, which can be impractical or hazardous when working with corrosive or toxic materials. Maintaining a controlled environment during testing further complicates measurements, as even minor contamination can alter results. Together, these challenges create a significant barrier to obtaining reliable data on fluid behavior in systems where precise performance understanding is essential. Problems Solved: ThermaSpin High-Temperature Viscometer addresses these challenges by providing a sealed, high-temperature measurement system that can operate reliably in extreme environments while maintaining strict control over sample purity. Its rotational design, coupled with a highly sensitive torsion-based measurement approach, enables accurate detection of the very low forces associated with low-viscosity molten fluids�something conventional instruments struggle to achieve. The enclosed architecture allows operation under inert or controlled atmospheres, preventing contamination from air or moisture, while also supporting smaller sample sizes to reduce risk and material constraints. By integrating temperature resilience, corrosion compatibility and precise mechanical measurement into a single platform, ThermaSpin overcomes the key technical and practical limitations that have historically restricted viscosity characterization in these demanding conditions. Key Advantages: Extreme temperature capability (~1000�C): Reliable operation for molten salts, metals and other high-temperature fluids High sensitivity for low-viscosity liquids: Accurately captures subtle flow behavior that conventional viscometers miss Sealed, controlled environment: Maintains sample purity by preventing exposure to air and moisture Handles corrosive and hazardous materials: Durable design compatible with chemically aggressive substances and smaller sample sizes No specialized infrastructure required: Eliminates dependence on costly, limited-access techniques like neutron imaging Versatile and integration-ready: Adaptable to multiple applications and compatible with inert atmosphere systems (e.g., glove boxes) Market Applications: Advanced Nuclear Energy: Molten salt reactors (MSRs), fusion systems and fuel cycle development Thermal Energy Storage & CSP: High-temperature heat transfer and storage fluids for renewable energy systems Metallurgy & Metal Processing: Molten metal monitoring in refining, casting and advanced manufacturing Chemical Processing: High-temperature and corrosive fluid handling in industrial chemical production Research & Development: National labs, academia and industry studying thermophysical properties of extreme-condition materials Defense & Government Applications: Controlled characterization of hazardous or sensitive molten materials in secure environments Development Status: TRL 3 US Patent pending LA-UR-26-26227 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Scan-to-Sample
description: Imagine loading an irregular block of metal, or a finished curved part, into a single station and walking away with precisely cut samples, no specialized machining expertise required. Scan-to-Sample from Los Alamos National Laboratory makes that possible by weaving 3D scanning, design software and computer-guided cutting into one continuous digital thread, running from the first scan straight through to the finished part. The system captures the true shape of the starting material, however curved or complex, then plans and carries out the cuts on its own, sparing operators the slow, error-prone job of hand-aligning and re-zeroing equipment for every specimen. The payoff is faster turnaround, less wasted material and consistent, repeatable quality, bringing advanced machining within reach of a far wider range of users and parts. How it Works The workflow begins when a scanning device, such as a laser scanner, optical scanner or contact probe, captures the exact geometry of the incoming material or part and produces an accurate digital 3D model. Design software then imports that model, where an operator marks the locations, orientations and sizes of the samples or features wanted, and the software calculates the tool paths needed to reach them. Those tool paths are converted into machine instructions, typically a G-code file, and loaded onto a computer numerical control machine, which secures the material and cuts the specimens by following the programmed paths without manual re-zeroing. After cutting, the finished part can be scanned again and compared against the original model to confirm that every specimen meets the required tolerances. Technical Description At its core, Scan-to-Sample links four cooperating elements: i) a scanning device that records the dimensional, geometric and surface characteristics of the workpiece; ii) an operations device that builds a watertight 3D model and generates the cutting program; iii) a machining apparatus such as a multi-axis CNC mill, turning center, grinder, laser or wire EDM system; and iv) a monitoring apparatus that verifies the outcome. The operations device applies a sample extraction model, which carries the functionality of standard CAD and CAM tools, to the 3D model so as to map sampling locations onto the true contours of the part and to derive the tool paths, cutting tools, spindle speeds, feed rates and fixturing choices suited to the material and its tolerances. Because the pipeline is driven by the scanned geometry rather than by fixed programming, it adapts to each unique part and supports two complementary modes of use. In sampling mode, the system extracts small test specimens from complex, non-linear components such as turbine blades or gear teeth, for mechanical testing and analysis. In fabrication mode, the same approach reads a raw or partially formed blank, billet or bar and produces a finished component from it, giving users an experience similar to the guided interfaces common in additive manufacturing. A closed feedback step compares the machined result against the digital model, allowing the system to flag deviations, take an additional sample or stop safely, which keeps quality consistent across every run. Advantages � Removes the slow, error-prone need to align and re-zero the machine by hand for every sample � Lowers the skill barrier, letting users with little machining experience produce complex parts � Handles irregular and curved stock that is hard to fixture and cut by conventional means � Reduces material waste when many small parts are taken from a single piece � Consolidates scanning, design and machining into one connected workflow � Improves precision, repeatability and sample yield across multiple runs Market Applications � Aerospace and Space Systems (turbine blade sampling, launch and propulsion component fabrication) � Power Generation and Energy (gear and turbine component testing) � Materials Research (mechanical behavior specimens for characterization) � Precision Manufacturing (custom parts from irregular or raw stock) � Automotive (drivetrain and gear inspection) � Quality Assurance and Metrology (dimensional verification and defect analysis) TRL 4 US Patent pending LA-UR-26-29796 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. title: Bulgaria – Repair and maintenance services of medical and precision equipment – ДСП Абонаментно сервизно обслужване на медицинска апаратура за УМБАЛ „Св. Иван Рилски“ ЕАД
description: ДСП - Абонаментно сервизно обслужване на медицинска апаратура съгасно първоначално планиран спектър /част от документацията за участие/ с посочено естество и количество на апаратурата, както и прогнозна стойност. Първоначално планиранираният спектър може да бъде частично изменен, както и да се добавя нова апаратура в хода на динамичната система. Одобрените кандидати могат да подадат оферта за една или повече единици, както и могат да не подадат оферта. ДСП функционира на два етапа: -Първи етап - събиране на заявления за участие (Краен срок за подаване на първоначални заявления - 10.05.2024 г.); -Втори етап - събиране на оферти по конкретни покани. Разглеждането на първоначалните заявления за участие ще се извърши в срок до 15 работни дни от крайният срок за подаване на заявления. Покана за конкретна поръчка няма да бъде обявявана преди да бъдат разгледани всички първоначални заявления. Заявления могат да се подават и след крайния срок за подаване на първоначални заявления, в тези случаи кандидатите ще получават покани след одобряване на включването им в ДСП. Офертите ще бъдат класирани от програма, която ще е достъпна и безплатна за всички кандидати. Осигурен е неограничен, пълен и пряк достъп до документацията за обществената поръчка през целия срок на действие на ДСП. ДСП ще функционира в рамките на три години, а именно в рамките на три години възложителят може да отправя покани до допуснатите кандидати за събиране на оферти за абонаментно сервизно обслужване на медицинска апаратура включена в първоначално планираният спектър или извън него. Слючените договори ще са със срок на действие 24 месеца, считано от влизането му в сила, който срок може да се удължи с нови 12 месеца. Естеството на услугите по абонаментно сервизно обслужване, които ще се извършват, включва извършването на профилактика и всички аварийни и текущи ремонти, при необходимост, на специализираната апаратура, както и подмяна на части, при необходимост.

title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: PinPoint Photon
description: Single Photon Generation Through Mechanical Deformation Value Proposition PinPoint Photon from Los Alamos National Laboratory gives quantum technology developers something they have long lacked: single photon sources that appear exactly where a designer places them. The approach relies on a wafer-scale film of an ultra-thin semiconductor shaped over precisely patterned tips. Light emitters can therefore be arranged in predictable arrays rather than found by chance. Early testing produced emitters at nearly nine out of 10 tip sites, with stable output for hours and excited-state lifetimes many times longer than those of unstrained material. Hardware teams in secure communications, photonic computing and quantum sensing gain a practical path from laboratory demonstrations to manufacturable chips. Challenges Many emerging quantum technologies need light that arrives one photon at a time. Examples include encryption keys that cannot be intercepted unnoticed and optical quantum computers. Ultra-thin 2D materials such as tungsten diselenide, tungsten disulfide and hexagonal boron nitride can produce such photons, but only from defects that form randomly, with no reliable way to control their location. Earlier attempts to guide emission by patterning the surface underneath the film could not separate the effect of mechanical strain from changes in the surrounding material, so the underlying physics stayed unclear. Most 2D quantum materials have also come from lab-scale methods such as peeling flakes off a crystal, which are unsuitable for large-scale device integration. Secure communication systems further need each site to hold no more than one emitter, a level of control that random defects cannot provide. Problems Solved PinPoint Photon replaces chance with design. A continuous few-layer tungsten diselenide film grown by gas-source chemical vapor deposition is transferred onto an array of ultra-sharp silicon dioxide tips. Each tip bends the film enough to localize emission at its apex. The film sits in a uniform silicon dioxide environment, so the team showed that mechanical bending alone creates the emission sites. That result answers the open scientific question left by earlier studies. The vapor deposition process is compatible with wafer-scale integration, and designers can set tip spacing so that each emitter remains individually accessible to optical systems. The resulting emitters showed no fine structure splitting, a key advance for quantum applications, along with spectral stability and roughly an order of magnitude longer lifetime than free excitons. Measured single photon purity reached about 70% at 3.8 K, with stable emission for up to eight hours. Advantages Places quantum light sources at chosen locations instead of random ones High success rate, with emitters forming at 87% of tip sites in testing Built on a wafer-scale growth process suited to chip-style manufacturing Steady, long-lived light output that held stable for hours Clean emission without the line splitting that complicates many quantum emitters Potentially extends to other 2D materials emitting from the ultraviolet to the infrared Market Applications Quantum Communications (secure key distribution, quantum networks, encrypted links) Quantum Computing (photonic processors, all-optical quantum circuits) Photonic Integrated Circuits and Semiconductors (on-chip light sources, optical signal generation) Sensing and Metrology (magnetic field sensors, temperature sensors) Scientific Instrumentation (quantum optics test sources, research tools for universities and laboratories) TRL 3 U.S. Patent No. 12,237,428 LA-UR-26-29956 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: GasFlow DLP Printing Interface
description: GasFlow DLP Printing Interface, developed by scientists at Los Alamos National Laboratory, helps resin-based 3D printing systems produce finer details, faster builds and more consistent part quality by controlling oxygen where curing happens most critically. The open-surface approach fits well with bottom-up DLP and related vat photopolymer processes, and it can enhance existing printer designs, as well as new platforms, by improving print fidelity, process stability and material flexibility. How it Works The system adds a second liquid beneath the printable resin inside the vat, creating a stable fluid-fluid interface between the two liquids. This interface is where the resin is polymerized, removing the need to pull the polymerized layer off the surface - an inherent default in the DLP process. The lower liquid is chosen to be an immiscible, high-density fluid, such as a perfluorinated fluid, that is treated with an inert gas and circulated continuously during printing. As it flows beneath the resin and above the transparent vat window, the lower liquid removes oxygen from the resin and introduces inert gas in its place, which reduces oxygen inhibition at the curing zone. With less oxygen interfering with polymerization, projected light can cure smaller features more reliably, more quickly and more uniformly across the part with less bleeding. Technical Description The patented GasFlow DLP Printing Interface is designed for additive manufacturing methods such as DLP, SLA and related photopolymer printing processes. The GasFlow DLP Printing Interface uses a first container or vat with a transparent portion, a first fluid positioned against that transparent portion and a second fluid that serves as the printable resin. The first fluid and second fluid form a fluid-fluid interface, with the first fluid located between the vat window and the resin. A circulation system moves the first fluid through the vat and an associated treatment container by way of conduits and a pumping mechanism. In representative embodiments, the first fluid is a perfluorinated solvent that has been treated with an inert gas such as nitrogen, helium, argon or carbon dioxide. As the treated first fluid circulates, it removes oxygen from resin at the interface and helps replace that oxygen with inert gas, which improves polymerization performance at the print surface. Oxygen in standard resin systems can suppress curing, which means more energy is required than necessary which in turn can create uneven polymerization that leaves parts overcured in some regions and undercured in others making very small features difficult to print. Features below about 50 microns in diameter may fail to print when normal oxygen levels are present. GasFlow DLP Printing demonstrated print speed improvement of at least one-third, with larger gains considered possible under optimized conditions. An added benefit to flowing fluid is that the system can provide temperature-control to help manage heat buildup during printing, which can improve part quality and widen the range of usable resin chemistries. Advantages Produces finer features and higher print resolution Reduces oxygen-related defects during curing Speeds printing compared with standard setups (oxygen exposed) Improves consistency across the part, including edge-to-center uniformity Supports retrofit potential for many bottom-up DLP printers Increases lifetime of liquid resin May enable use of resin chemistries that are otherwise difficult to process because of overheating or curing instability Market Applications Additive Manufacturing (resin 3D printers, printer upgrades, production platforms) Industrial Manufacturing (precision polymer parts, lightweight structures, fabrication tooling) Medical and Dental (custom polymer components, device fabrication, detailed models) Electronics and Microfabrication (fine-feature polymer structures, patterned parts, prototyping) Research and Laboratory Equipment (materials development, process testing, advanced printing systems) Aerospace and Defense (complex geometries, lattice structures, specialty components) TRL 4 US Patent No. 11,911,955 LA-UR-26-29477 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. The dredge shall be complete in all respects, including all attendant plant, equipment, and crew necessary to perform the required dredging operations. The estimated magnitude of construction for this project is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 237990, with a small business size standard of $37,000,000. This acquisition will be procured as Full and Open Competition. Market research indicates that while small business dredging firms exist within NAICS 237990, there is not a reasonable expectation that two or more responsible small business concerns possess the required dredge plant size, pumping capacity, and operational capability to perform this work at fair market prices. The solicitation is anticipated to be issued on or about 7 April 2026 , with a bid opening date to be established in a future amendment. The solicitation documents will be posted on SAM.gov (www.sam.gov). Interested vendors are encouraged to register as an Interested Vendor on SAM.gov. description: 1. Обект и предмет: Обект на динамичната система за покупки (ДСП) е „доставка“ по смисъла на чл. 3, ал. 1, т. 2 от ЗОП. Предмет на ДСП: „Доставка на лекарствени продукти, които не са включени в Приложение 2 на ПЛС, за нуждите на МБАЛ „Д-р Христо Стамболски „ЕООД гр.Казанлък“ Лекарствените продукти са посочени по редове и са подробно представени по лекарствени форми, количество лекарствено вещество, единица мярка и необходимо прогнозно количество в приложената към документацията първоначална „Техническа спецификация“. Първоначално планираната "Техническа спецификация" може да бъде частично променяна в хода на провеждане на динамичната система, като се добавят нови лекарствени продукти и/или се променят количествата им. Посочените количества в приложената към документацията „Техническа спецификация“ са прогнозни и не пораждат задължение за Възложителя да ги възложи в прогнозния обем. 2. Срок на динамичната система за покупки: Срокът на ДСП е 24 /двадесет и четири/ месеца. Динамичната система за покупки е отворена през целия си срок на действие за всеки кандидат, който отговаря на критериите за подбор. Достъпът и участието в нея са свободни и безплатни за всички заинтересовани лица. Срок на договорите, сключвани въз основа на ограничените поръчки в рамките на ДСП е за период от 12 /дванадесет месеца/ месеца, като крайният срок за изпълнение на договорите може да бъде удължен въз основа на едностранно писмено уведомление от страна на ВЪЗЛОЖИТЕЛЯ до приключване на следваща процедура за възлагане на обществена поръчка и сключване на нов договор със същия предмет или при наличие на условията на чл.116 ал.1 т.3 от ЗОП, но за не повече от 6 месеца . 3. Място на изпълнение на поръчката: Всички лекарствени продукти се доставят франко Болничната аптека на МБАЛ „Д-р Христо Стамболски „ЕООД , ул. „Старозагорска“ 16 , гр.Казанлък. ​​​​​​​

title: Former General Leonard Wood Army Community Hospital (FGLWACH) Pre-Demolition Environmental Survey
description: Former General Leonard Wood Army Community Hospital (FGLWACH) Pre-Demolition Environmental SurveyFort Leonard Wood, MO W912DQ26RA082 CONTRACT INFORMATION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Kansas City District (NWK) intends solicit, negotiate, and award a one-time Small Business Set Aside, Firm-Fixed-Price, Architect-Engineer (AE) contract to complete a thorough inspection of all identified buildings. The inspection is required to identify the presence, location, and quantities of potentially hazardous and other regulated materials that will require either abatement or special disposal requirements when the FGLWACH is demolished. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 541330 Engineering Services The Product Service Code (PSC) is C219 Architect and Engineering-General: Other Small Business Size Standard is $25.5 million Estimated Magnitude of the Service: Between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000 The requirement is being set-aside for Small Businesses. The actual solicitation will be posted and available on SAM.gov on or about 30 April 2026. Proposals will be due approximately 30 days later. The solicitation and any issued amendments will include the proposal submission and evaluation criteria, and shall establish the actual proposal due date. Viewing and download the solicitation requires registration at the SAM.gov website at https://sam.gov/. Downloads and instructions are available through this website. Any amendments will only be available from this website. Offerors are responsible for checking the website frequently for any update(s) to this Pre-Solicitation Announcement or amendments to the Solicitation. Synopsis of the Scope of Work:The FGLWACH is scheduled to be demolished. This demolition effort shall consist of the complete removal of the following buildings, Hospital and Clinic (B310), Central Utility Plant (B311), associated Infectious Waste Storage structure, Ambulance Garage, and Temporary Helipad. The tasks include verifying current information provided in the AE-0 Planning Study and updating information in the Pre-Demolition Inspection Report. Assess the Hospital and Clinic, Central Utility Plant, associated Infectious Waste Storage structure, and Ambulance Garage for additional asbestos and other regulated material through destructive testing as needed. Provide any information on types, quantities, and locations of any hazardous material in the Pre-Demolition Inspection Report. Identify any storage tank locations, contents, and if any leakage has occurred. Provide information in the Pre-Demolition Inspection Report. Prior to demolition activities, the Contractor must complete a thorough inspection of all identified buildings. This inspection is required to identify the presence, location, and quantities of potentially hazardous and other regulated materials that will require either abatement or special disposal requirements when those buildings are demolished. Following inspection, the Contractor shall be able to completely quantify the hazardous and regulated materials present and shall identify and describe the abatement methods required to remove and dispose of said materials, to include any special demolition procedures and worker safety measures. The inspection of the buildings must use destructive techniques typically required to access and inspect exterior/interior walls and hidden areas, where hazards may be present, such as behind wall coverings, wallboards, insulation, baseboards, etc. All sampling and testing shall be planned and performed in accordance with Federal and State regulations for that specific location; and destructive sampling is authorized to access hidden and covered areas.

title: Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) Airborne Systems Integration (ASI) Division
description: Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Lakehurst, NJ in support of Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) Airborne Systems Integration (ASI) Division is soliciting white papers/proposals for research and development support in technologies that are applicable to the following: air platforms, manned and unmanned payloads, advanced computing and processing, air platform support systems, advanced air system security and protection, and improved Naval air capabilities. Example focus areas include improved technologies, techniques or advanced applications of communications, Electro-Optical (EO), Infrared (IR), Radio Frequency (RF), acoustic and non-acoustic sensors, persistent surveillance technologies, and special sensor systems for Navy manned aircraft and Unmanned Air Systems (UAS). The NAWCAD WOLF ASI Division develops advanced air platforms, sensors (e.g., acoustics, EO/IR, radar, magnetics, and other special sensors), and systems to meet current and future Naval capability demands. The purpose of these platforms, sensors and systems is to support a variety of aviation missions including distributed maritime surveillance, Air Undersea Warfare (USW), airborne strike, air warfare, counter-air, close air support and interdiction, defense suppression, advanced communications, digital interoperability, electronic attack, naval warfare and amphibious strike, Counter Unmanned Systems (C-UxS), anti-surface warfare, and contested logistic support. Most of the air platforms will be small Group 1 to Group 4 UAS or modifications to existing larger manned and unmanned air platforms. Sensors could be air deployed (via manned or unmanned aircraft), ground, surface, or undersea deployable as driven by the mission needs. Advanced computing and processing will be focused on air vehicle, payload, edge computing, artificial intelligence and machine learning, or multi-platform collaborative solutions supporting all aspects of mission information from pre-deployment, through operations, to post deployment and sustainment. Advanced air system security and protection will be focused on securing information, transmissions, anti-tampering, and reduced probability of compromise of existing technologies or technologies in development. Improved naval capabilities will focus on key naval focus areas or capability gaps supporting improved lethality, availability, and affordability. This BAA not only includes air vehicle systems, mission systems, sensors, sensor data processing, and sensor systems, but it also includes mathematical modeling of the sensors and air platforms, communication techniques between the sensors and/or platforms, interfaces, software development, the fusion and exploitation of multi-sensor data, studies, artificial intelligence, deep learning, machine learning, advanced algorithms, and other techniques used to develop advanced capabilities and reduce the cost of transitioning sensors technologies to the fleet. Furthermore, this BAA shall cover development and analysis of related air, sea, and land detection models using relevant data.

title: Ibuprofen 400MG/ 600MG/ 800MG Presolicitation
description: The Defense Logistics Agency is planning to issue a solicitation for a national requirements contract for Ibuprofen Tablets. Procurement details follow. Ibuprofen 400MG in 30, 90 and 500 count bottles and Ibuprofen 600MG and 800MG in 90 and 500 count bottles. This will be an unrestricted and fully competitive acquisition. The contract will be a firm-fixed price, requirements type contract with a one year base and four one year options. A contract resulting from this solicitation will establish a national supply source, in accordance with FAR 52.216-21 (Requirements), to provide the items listed in the schedule for purchase by Department of Defense, Department of Veterans Affairs, Indian Health Service and Bureau of Prisons customers through the DLA and VA prime vendor programs. The annual usage estimates will be provided in the Schedule of Supplies section of the solicitation. This is a commercial item and will be solicited using FAR part 12. All sources may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the agency. A copy of the solicitation will be posted to the DLA Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil and Beta Sam.Gov at https://beta.sam.gov/. Interested parties should contact Kevin Rafferty (215-737-0907) (kevin.rafferty@dla.mil) for any questions/comments. Interested parties are further advised to set up automated notifications of pre-solicitation or solicitation changes through this website. The current projected solicitation date is April of 2021. DLA reserves the right to issue the solicitation before or after the projected solicitation date.

description: Tällä hankintailmoituksella perustetaan dynaaminen toimittajarekisteri tuottamaan vammaispalvelulain ja sosiaalihuoltolain mukaisia kuljetuksia Espoon kaupungille sekä Länsi-Uudenmaan alueella sijaitseville kunnille (Hanko, Inkoo, Kirkkonummi, Kauniainen, Lohja, Raasepori, Siuntio, ja Karviaisen Kuntayhtymä (sis. title: Updated List of Approved Labs to Conduct SD-STD-01.01 Forced Entry and Ballistic Resistance (FE/BR) Certification Testing
description: Background Information: The US Department of State, Bureau of Diplomatic Security (DS), has an established program to verify that specific building systems used in Diplomatic facilities constructed overseas protect building occupants. This is accomplished through a testing and certification protocol detailed in DS�s proprietary testing standard, SD-STD-01.01 Revision H (pub. June 16, 2020), Certification Standard, Forced Entry and Ballistic Resistance of Building Systems. New Update: The DS Office of Physical Security Programs, Physical Security Division, Research and Development Section (DS/PSD/RD) has recently updated the list of labs approved by the Department of State to conduct FE/BR certification testing. SD-STD-01.01 Rev H Table 8 (version 2): Commercial Test Labs Approved by DOS to Conduct FE and BR Tests to this Standard has been superseded by Table 8 (version 3): Commercial Test Labs Approved by DOS to Conduct FE and BR Tests to SD-STD-01.01, effective immediately. This update adds one additional testing laboratory to the approved list, Susquehanna Labs.. The list of approved FE/BR certification testing laboratories is subject to change at the Bureau of Diplomatic Security�s discretion. Testing facilities may be added to this list if they demonstrate their understanding of SD-STD-01.01, their ability to meet established industry practices, their ability to communicate effectively with DS/PSD/RD, and their ability and willingness to perform both forced-entry and ballistic certification testing. For general questions regarding this announcement and/or to obtain an electronic copy of SD-STD-01.01, Revision H, v3, Certification Standard, Forced Entry and For general questions regarding this announcement and/or to obtain an electronic copy of SD-STD-01.01, Revision H, v3, Certification Standard, Forced Entry and Ballistic Resistance of Building Systems, please contact FEBRCerts@groups.state.gov.

title: Communications Headquarters Facility - DMAFB
description: This is a design build project to construct a 45,025SF Communications Squadron headquarters facility with reinforced concrete foundation, concrete slab, structural steel frame, standing seam metal roof and exterior. Portions of this facility must be constructed to comply with Intelligence Community Directive 705 criteria and standards. The facility should be compatible with applicable Department of Defense, Air Force, and base design standards. In addition, local materials and construction techniques shall be used where cost effective. The facility must be able to withstand wind loads and seismic effects as prescribed in applicable codes and design guides. The facility will include a 500KW generator which is authorized by the Air Force Manual 32-1062. The project will include all supporting facilities such as site improvements, utilities, communications, pavements, parking, and sidewalks necessary to provide a complete and useable facility. Facilities will be designed as permanent construction in accordance with Department of Defense Unified Facilities Criteria 1-200-01.This project will comply with Department of Defense antiterrorism/force protection requirements per Unified Facilities Criteria4-010-01.THIS PROJECT IS AN UNRESTRICTED REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), BEST VALUE TRADE-OFF. The procurement method used will be 1-step best value trade-off. Eligible offerors will be required to provide a technical and price proposal for consideration of award. The technical proposal will be evaluated based on the evaluation criteria stated in the RFP. When the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) uses a Best Value Trade-Off procurement, it is seeking to award a contract to the contractor that provides the greatest overall benefit in response to the requirement, not necessarily the one with the lowest price. This method allows for a tradeoff between non-cost factors and cost/price, and lets the Government accept a proposal that is not the lowest priced or the highest technically rated to achieve the best value. Evaluation Method: The project will be a negotiated procurement using the Best Value Trade-Off process to ensure a competitive, firm-fixed price contract. The solicitation will be available on or about 16 April 2026. The solicitation and all amendments for this acquisition will be posted on SAM.GOV, http://sam.gov/. It is the responsibility of the offerors to check the designated government point of entry - sam.gov - frequently for any amendments or changes to the solicitation. All Offerors are also advised that this procurement may be delayed, cancelled, or revised at any time during the solicitation, evaluation and/or final award processSubcontracting Goals:? The SDVOSB goal of (5% Subcontract value/3% Contract value) is reflective of the 2024 NDAA, number of SDVOSBs among the possible NAICS code scopes and past performance above? The WOSB goal is (5% Subcontract value/4% Contract) value given the high numbers of WOSBs within the NAICS codes of possible scopes in addition to WOSB past performance above.? The HUB goal is (1.5% Subcontract value/1% Contract) value given the very low numbers of HUBs within the NAICS codes of possible scopes in addition to the HUB past performance above.? description: Invitation for Bids (IFB) Set-Aside for Small BusinessesNAICS Code: 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering ConstructionThe 134th Air Refueling Wing of the Tennessee National Guard intends to issue an Invitation for Bids (IFB) to award a single firm-fixed-price contract for the repair of the perimeter security fencing at McGhee Tyson Air National Guard Base, Tennessee. This is a total small business set-aside.The scope of the project involves providing all necessary personnel, equipment, tools, materials, and supervision to repair the installations perimeter security fencing in accordance with the plans and specifications that will be provided with the solicitation. This project is critical to maintaining the physical security of the installation.The contract duration will be 365 calendar days from the date of the notice to proceed. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this project is 237990, with a corresponding small business size standard of $45,000,000. The estimated magnitude of construction is between $3,000,000 and $5,000,000.The tentative date for issuing the solicitation is on-or-about 19 May 2026. title: United States Coast Guard (CG) Waterfront Optimization at the Coast Guard Yard, Curtis Bay, Maryland
description: Pre-Solicitation Notice: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Baltimore District, plans to solicit the design and construction of the United States Coast Guard (CG) Waterfront Optimization at the Coast Guard Yard, Curtis Bay, Maryland. This project is critically necessary to prepare for the arrival, maintenance, and repair of a new class of CG Cutters (Offshore Patrol Cutter [OPC] and National Security Cutter [NSC]) at the Yard anticipated to arrive in 2030. This requirement will be solicited as a competitive, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract using a two-phase Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) methodology. The planned construction period is 1,005 calendar days. The Solicitation is scheduled to be released on/or about 6 May 2026.

title: Bulgaria – Pharmaceutical products – „Доставка на лекарствени продукти, които не са включени в Приложение 2 на ПЛС, за нуждите на УМБАЛ "КАНЕВ" АД
description: ДСП се създава за периодична доставка по предварителна заявка на лекарствени продукти, които не са включени в Приложение 2 на ПЛС по чл. 262, ал. 6, т. 2 от ЗЛПХМ, необходими за изпълнение на лечебната дейност в УМБАЛ „КАНЕВ” АД. Лекарствените продукти, предмет на процедурата са представени в първоначална "Техническа спецификация“ /част от документацията за участие/, с посочени лекарствени форми, количество лекарствено вещество, единица мярка и необходимо прогнозно количество. Първоначално планиранираната "Техническа спецификация" може да бъде частично променяна в хода на провеждане на динамичната система, като се добавят нови лекарствени продукти и/или се променят количествата им. Посочените количества в приложената към настоящите указания „Техническа спецификация“ са прогнозни и не пораждат задължение за Възложителя да ги възложи в прогнозния обем. Кандидатите, включени в ДСП могат да подадат оферта за един или повече редове, както и могат да не подадат оферта. ДСП ще функционира в рамките на 36 /тридесет и шест/ месеца, като в този период Възложителят може да отправя покани до включените в ДСП кандидати за събиране на оферти за всяка конкретна поръчка за доставка на лекарствени продукти, в рамките на ДСП. Срок на договорите, сключвани въз основа на ограничените поръчки в рамките на ДСП е за период от 24 месеца. ДСП функционира на два етапа, както следва: ПЪРВИ ЕТАП НА ДИНАМИЧНАТА СИСТЕМА ЗА ПОКУПКИ – СЪБИРАНЕ НА ЗАЯВЛЕНИЯ ЗА УЧАСТИЕ: Квалифициране на доставчиците (допускане на доставчиците до системата). На този етап се събират заявления за участие в ДСП. Заявленията за участие /ЕЕДОП/ съдържат информация относно личното състояние на кандидатите и критериите за подбор, поставени от Възложителя. Краен срок за подаване на първоначални заявления - 15.04.2024 г. Разглеждането на първоначалните заявления за участие се извършва в срок до 10 /десет/ работни дни от крайният срок за подаване на първоначални заявления, след което Възложителят определя с решение за подбор с което квалифицираните доставчици се включват в ДСП. След първоначалния срок за подаване на заявления, Възложителят ще разглежда новопостъпилите заявления два пъти в месеца /всеки понеделник от първата и третата седмица на месеца/. След всяко разглеждане на заявленията, Възложителят издава решение за подбор. След влизане в сила на решението за подбор следва втори етап на процедурата. ВТОРИ ЕТАП НА ДИНАМИЧНАТА СИСТЕМА ЗА ПОКУПКИ – СЪБИРАНЕ НА ОФЕРТИ ПО КОНКРЕТНИ ПОКАНИ: След влизане в сила на първоначалното решение за включване на одобрените кандидатите в ДСП, Възложителят обявява отделни процедури в рамките на ДСП. За всяка конкретна процедура, Възложителят изпраща покана за представяне на оферти за конкретната поръчка до всички кандидати, включени в ДСП. Офертите на кандидатите съдържат техническо и ценово предложение. Офертите ще бъдат класирани от програма, която ще бъде достъпна и безплатна за участниците.

title: Facility Investment Services
description: This is a PRESOLICITATION NOTICE, informing interested vendors of the intent to publish a solicitation for Facility Investment Services at Marine Corps Reserve Training Center, Kaneohe Bay, HI.. Classification: 8(a) set-aside PSC: Z1JZ NAICS: 561210 The work includes, but is not limited to, furnishing all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, incidental engineering, and other items necessary to provide Facility Investment Services at Marine Corps Reserve Training Center, Kaneohe Bay, HI. Facility Support Services include maintenance, repair, alteration, demolition and minor construction for the following: Building Systems -HVAC and Refrigeration Systems -Interior and Exterior Lighting Systems -Fire Protection Systems -Electrical Miscellaneous -Signs -Locks Procurement Method: Contracting by Negotiation. The NAICS Code for this procurement is 561210 and the annual size standard is $47 million. The contract term will be for a one-year base period plus four one-year option periods and one six-month option period, for a maximum duration of 66 months. The Government will not synopsize the options when exercised. Non-recurring work may be issued via FedMall, a web-based ordering system, using Government purchase cards. The previous contract is currently in the 8(a) program. Based on market research, including a sources sought notice issued to the Small Business Administration (SBA) in February 2026, there is a reasonable expectation that offers would be obtained from at least two responsible 8(a) concerns. Eight firms provided the requested information and appear capable of providing the required services, with three being 8(a) firms. Based on the results, the requirement will remain in the 8(a) program and the solicitation will be issued as an 8(a) competitive set-aside. NAVFAC Hawaii�s Office of Small Business Programs concurs with the set-aside determination. All interested Offerors shall register in PIEE. No notice of solicitation activity will be provided to interested Offerors. Proposal receipt date TBD

description: The Marine Corps Installations National Capital Region-Regional Contracting Office (MCINCR-RCO), Quantico, VA, has a requirement to provide program management, instructional services, subject matter expert /curriculum development services, editorial services, multimedia expertise, instructional technology, administrative services, and student support services in support of the Marine Corps University (MCU) Center for Distance Education (CDET) Distance Professional Military Education (DPME) program Academic Support Services. This support is to be provided at the CDET Headquarters in Quantico, VA and mainly at the seven (7) regional Campus and office locations: ? MCB Quantico, VA, ? MCB Camp Lejeune, NC, ? MCB Camp Pendleton, CA, ? Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS), Miramar, CA, ? Joint Reserve Base (JRB), Fort Worth, TX, ? MCB Kaneohe Bay, HI, and ? MCB Camp Butler, Okinawa, Japan. This is a follow-on contract of Seaport NxG task order M67854-21-F-3009. It is the Government?s intention to issue a single award hybrid Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) consisting of Firm Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract Line Items for services and Cost Reimbursement for travel. The contract will have a five-year ordering period and a total ceiling value of about $153M. The ordering period is estimated to commence on 3rd Quarter 2027. The proposed acquisition will be procured as a 100% set aside to Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 611710. The Government will solicit and award utilizing commercial contracting under FAR Part 12 using FAR 15- Contracting by Negotiation. The Government intends to award using best value. The award will be issued on an all or none basis. The draft Performance Work Statement is posted with the synopsis and is made available on the web site https://www.sam.gov. It is the responsibility of the interested offerors to continually view the website for the solicitation and any amendments. Contractors interested in doing business with the Government must be registered with the SAM website accessed through https://www.sam.gov. Contractor must also ensure annual representations and certifications are current or complete them at the SAM website as well. All prospective quoters interested in submitting a quote must have a commercial and government entity code (CAGE code). Contractors must be registered with Wide Area Workflow at https://piee.eb.mil/. description: This announcement constitutes a Pre-Solicitation notice (SYNOPSIS) in accordance with FAR Subpart 5.2. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Honolulu District hereby announces its intent to issue a solicitation entitled, ?Relocate Schofield Barracks Deep Wells Above Ground, Building 1580, Schofield Barracks, Oahu, Hawaii? as described within this announcement. This project is a Design-Bid-Build solicitation, utilizing Best Value Trade Off (BVTO) procedures in accordance with FAR Part 15. The Government intends to solicit this requirement as unrestricted procurement. The North American Industry Classification code (NAICS) for this requirement is 237110. The Small Business size standard for this NAICS code is $45,000,000 annual average revenue. The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-price construction contract as a result of this solicitation. September with consideration for the largest pump to be on stand-by. Motors to be located above ground. Each well, pump, motor sized to deliver a minimum of 2,000 gallons per minute. description: ДСП се създава за доставка на различни видове реактиви, медицински изделия и консумативи за нуждите на МБАЛ " Д-р Тота Венкова“ АД. Първоначално планиранираната "Техническа спецификация" може да бъде частично променяна в хода на провеждане на динамичната система, като се добавят нови реактиви, консумативи и/или медицински изделия и/или се променят количествата им. Посочените количества в приложената към документацията „Техническа спецификация“ са прогнозни и не пораждат задължение за Възложителя да ги възложи в прогнозния обем. Фактическото изпълнение на обществената поръчка ще се определи на базата на реално доставените реактиви, медицински изделия и консумативи, в рамките на финансовия ресурс. Обменът на документи и съобщения между Възложители, кандидати, участници и изпълнители на обществени поръчки се осъществява чрез Централизираната електронна платформа. Срокът на ДСП е 36 месеца. Динамичната система за покупки е отворена през целия си срок на действие за всеки кандидат, който отговаря на критериите за подбор. Достъпът и участието в нея са свободни и безплатни за всички заинтересовани лица. Срок на договорите, сключвани въз основа на ограничените поръчки в рамките на ДСП е за период от 12 /дванадесет/ месеца. Динамичната система за покупки (ДСП) се провежда на етапи. Съгласно чл.101 от ЗОП, в зависимост от етапа на процедурата кандидатите подават заявления за участие, а квалифицираните (допуснати) кандидати - оферти. ДСП се управлява като изцяло електронен процес и през целия срок на действие на системата за покупки тя е открита за всеки стопански субект /изпълняващ орган/ИО/, който отговаря на критериите за подбор. Посочените критерии за подбор, са и критерии за изключване. Възложителят осигурява пълен, неограничен и пряк достъп до документацията по настоящата процедура чрез Централизираната електронна платформа, наричана "платформата". Заявлениятаи офертите трябва да се изготвят и представят в съответствие с изискванията на чл. 101 от ЗОП и чл.47 от ППЗОП, в срока посочен в обявлението. Всяко заявление и Всяка оферта се подава в системата на ЦАИС ЕОП Първи етап /първоначално събиране на заявления за участие/: Квалифициране на доставчиците (допускане на доставчиците до системата). На този етап се събират заявления за участие. Заявленията за участие /ЕЕДОП/ съдържа/т информация относно личното състояние на кандидатите и критериите за подбор. Краен срок за подаване на първоначални заявления - 23.05.2024 г. Разглеждането на първоначалните заявления за участие ще се извърши в срок до 10 работни дни от крайният срок за подаване на първоначални заявления. Покана за конкретна поръчка няма да бъде обявявана преди да бъдат разгледани всички първоначални заявления. Заявления могат да се подават и след крайния срок за подаване на първоначални заявления, в тези случаи кандидатите ще получават покани след одобряване на включването им в ДСП. Възложителят определя с Решение за подбор квалифицираните доставчици. След влизане в сила на Решението за подбор следва втори етап на процедурата. Втори етап /събиране на оферти по конкретни покани/: Следва изпращане на покана за представяне на оферти за конкретна обществена поръчка до тези доставчици, които са били квалифицирани/допуснати. Офертите съдържат техническо и ценово предложение. Съгласно чл.39, ал.1 от ППЗОП с подаването на оферта се счита, че кандидатите се съгласяват с всички условия на възложителя, в т.ч. с определения от него срок на валидност на офертите и с проекта на договор. Покана за конкретна поръчка няма да бъде обявявана преди да бъдат разгледани всички първоначални заявления, подадени в посоченият по-горе срок. При конкретни поръчки по покани офертите ще бъдат класирани от програма, която ще е достъпна и безплатна за всички кандидати. Осигурен е неограничен, пълен и пряк достъп до документацията за обществената поръчка през целия срок на действие на ДСП. *По всяко време заинтересовани лица могат да подават заявления за допускане/включване в ДСП. Възложителят ще разглежда новопостъпилите предложения два пъти в месеца (1-во и 15-то число на месеца) или на две седмици веднъж. Възложителят ще издава решение за допускане на кандидатите в ДСП. След всяко разглеждане на заявленията Възложителят издава Решение за подбор с което квалифицираните доставчици се присъединяват към ДСП.

title: Department of Commerce (DOC) Cloud Services Provider Vehicle Strategy
description: 1. Notice of Strategy The Department of Commerce (DOC) is providing this notice to inform industry of its procurement strategy for the Cloud Vehicle Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA). This 10-year vehicle, with an estimated value of $4.105 Billion, is designed to provide native hyperscale cloud services across the Department. 2. Direct-to-CSP Approach Due to highly specialized technical requirements, including massive compute elasticity (25,000+ concurrent vCPUs), proprietary 100+ Tbps global backbones, and specific hardware density for AI/ML and weather modeling, the Department is utilizing a Direct-to-CSP strategy. It is contemplated that to ensure mission success and direct engineering support, only Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) acting as the Cloud Service Provider (CSP) will be eligible for award. 3. Authority This strategy is being executed via GSA eBuy under the authority of GSAR Subpart 538.71. Participation is restricted to authorized contractors holding a GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) under SIN 518210C. 4. No Action Required This notice is for informational purposes only to ensure transparency in the Department's long-term cloud acquisition planning. The Department is not seeking quotes, proposals, or feedback as part of this notice. 5. Points of Contact Eric Olmstead, Contracting Officer: eric.olmstead@noaa.gov

title: Hungary – Computer equipment and supplies – Informatikai beszerzés DBR 2024
description: Dinamikus beszerzési rendszer (DBR) létrehozása informatikai eszközök, kellékek, szoftver licencek és kapcsolódó szolgáltatások beszerzésére a Budapest Gyógyfürdő és Hévízei Zrt. részére. Az ajánlatkérő által a DBR működtetésének időtartama (2 év) alatt megrendelni kívánt teljes mennyiség becsült értéke: 110.000.000 Ft. A DBR keretében odaítélendő egyes szerződések várható maximális nagyságrendje nem haladja meg a 90.000.000,- Ft-ot. Az ajánlatkérő ugyanakkor felhívja a figyelmet arra, hogy az eljárás nem keletkeztet részére lehívási kötelezettséget, továbbá a kategóriánként meghatározott nettó becsült értékek tervezett nagyságrendet jelentenek, Ajánlatkérő az ajánlattételi szakaszokban ettől eltérhet. Kategóriák (Kbt. 106.§ (4) bekezdésére tekintettel) 1. Számítógépek, szerverek, perifériák és kapcsolódó szolgáltatások Asztali számítógépek, tartozékaik és alkatrészeik, hordozható számítógépek és tartozékaik, egyéb informatikai eszközök, televíziók, kijelzők és tartozékaik, kiegészítők, projektorok és tartozékaik, alkatrészek, kiegészítők, interaktív táblák, kijelzők és kiegészítői és oktatástechnikai eszközök hozzá tartozó szolgáltatásokkal, szerverek, adattárolók és alkatrészek, tartozékok, meglévő IT eszközállományhoz egyéb alkatrészek, kellékek, adathordozók; Becsült érték: 58 millió Ft 2. Hálózati, biztonságtechnikai és telekommunikációs eszközök és kapcsolódó szolgáltatások Hálózati aktív és passzív eszközök, kellékek, alkatrészek; biztonságtechnikai eszközök; telekommunikációs eszközök; Becsült érték: 14 millió Ft 3. Kis/nagyteljesítményű nyomat előállító eszközök. Kellék- és alkatrészanyagok és kapcsolódó szolgáltatások Kis/nagyteljesítményű nyomat előállító eszközök (min. 25 lap/perc színes és fekete-fehér nyomtatás + fénymásolás, és scanelés funkció), tonerek, festékpatronok kellék és alkatrész nyomtatókhoz és fénymásoló berendezésekhez; Becsült érték: 13 millió Ft 4. Szoftverek és licencek IT biztonsági szoftverek, tűzfalak, operációs rendszerek, irodai alkalmazások, szoftverlicencek, adatbáziskezelők, virtualizációs szoftverlicenszek; Becsült érték: 15 millió Ft 5. Audiovizuális eszközök, szünetmentes áramforrások, és kapcsolódó kellékek, szolgáltatások Kamerák, fényképezőgépek és tartozékai, audio/Video eszközök, kellékek, elem, akkumulátor, töltők, szünetmentes áramforrások; Becsült érték: 5 millió Ft 6. A kategóriákhoz tartozó szolgáltatási elemek Installáció, üzemeltetés, bevizsgálás, hibaelhárítás, support, tanácsadás, fejlesztés; Becsült érték: 5 millió Ft A termékkategóriák további jellemzőit, az eszközök műszaki leírását a műszaki leírás tartalmazza. Ajánlatkérő a DBR működtetése során a Kbt. 107. § (2) bekezdés alapján a rendszerben megvalósítandó konkrét közbeszerzésekre vonatkozó pontos műszaki tartalmat és szerződéses feltételeket a DBR-ben részt vevő gazdasági szereplők számára az ajánlattételi felhívás(ok) megküldésével egyidejűleg bocsátja rendelkezésre. Ennek/ezek keretében Ajánlatkérő meghatározza, hogy a konkrét közbeszerzésbe tartozó termékek, eszközök mely termékkategóriá(k)ba tartoznak. Ajánlatkérő a Kbt. 107. § (2) bekezdése alapján fenntartja a jogot arra, hogy a DBR megvalósítása során az ajánlattételi felhívás megküldésével egyidejűleg, az abban foglalt konkrét beszerzés igényre vonatkozóan a konkrét közbeszerzések tárgyától és jellegétől függően részajánlattételi lehetőségeket határozzon meg.

title: VALVE,FLOAT,AIRCRAF
PITCH LOCK ACTUATOR
ATR Plant Protection System (PPS) Seismic Switch Replacement
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), the management and operating contractor for the U.S. Department of Energy-owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified suppliers capable of providing environmentally and seismically qualified seismic switches for use in the Advanced Test Reactor (ATR) Plant Protection System (PPS). The purpose of this EOI is to identify suppliers with the technical capability, quality assurance program, testing facilities, and experience necessary to provide safety-related seismic switch equipment qualified for nuclear applications. This EOI is being issued for market research and acquisition planning purposes and is intended to identify potential suppliers for a future procurement opportunity. The EOI process is used by INL to develop a list of qualified and interested vendors that may be considered for future solicitations. BACKGROUND The ATR Plant Protection System currently utilizes seismic switches to provide a critical reactor protection function. Seismic switches detect ground motion and initiate a reactor scram when predetermined seismic thresholds are exceeded. The existing Kinemetrics Model TS-3A seismic switches are obsolete and have demonstrated performance degradation, resulting in increased reliance on limited spare inventory. Additionally, one seismic switch is currently out of service, placing the PPS in a reduced logic configuration. Replacement with modern, supported equipment is required to restore normal system configuration and ensure long-term reliability and maintainability. SCOPE OF INTEREST BEA seeks information from suppliers capable of providing complete seismic switch solutions meeting the functional, environmental, seismic qualification, testing, documentation, and quality assurance requirements typically associated with nuclear safety-related applications. Functional Capability Three-axis ground motion sensing capability. Dry contact output suitable for reactor protection system input. Adjustable seismic trip setpoints. Response times consistent with nuclear protection system applications. Long-term reliability and maintainability. In-situ testing and calibration capabilities. Environmental and Seismic Qualification Respondents should be capable of qualifying equipment consistent with applicable industry standards, including IEEE 603 IEEE 323 IEEE 344 ANSI/ISA-67.04.01 ASME NQA-1 Deliverables Suppliers should be capable of providing: Complete seismic switch assemblies. Required mounting hardware and accessories. Qualification documentation and test reports. Operation and maintenance manuals. Installation and interface documentation. Calibration and surveillance procedures. Certificates of conformance and applicable certifications. MINIMUM MANDATORY CAPABILITIES To facilitate evaluation, respondents should clearly identify whether they can meet the following minimum capabilities: Provide a seismic switch solution capable of detecting low-level seismic events suitable for reactor protection applications. Demonstrate environmental and seismic qualification in accordance with IEEE 323 and IEEE 344 methodologies. Maintain a Quality Assurance Program consistent with ASME NQA-1 requirements or equivalent controls. Support a qualified service life suitable for long-term nuclear facility operation. Provide qualification reports, testing documentation, calibration information, and supporting quality records. Provide long-term product support, maintenance recommendations, and obsolescence management. RESPONSE FORMAT AND SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested organizations shall submit a concise response demonstrating their qualifications, capabilities, and interest in supporting this requirement. Responses should be limited to approximately 10 pages, excluding product literature, drawings, certifications, and supporting quality documentation. Responses should include, at a minimum: Organization name, mailing address, and primary point of contact UEI and CAGE Code (if applicable) Business size and socio-economic classifications Technical capabilities Relevant experience Quality Assurance Program information Manufacturing and delivery capabilities Estimated lead times Assumptions, exceptions, or recommendations related to the requirement Responses shall be submitted electronically in PDF format to: Chase Egbert & Stacey Hill Email: Chase.Egbert@inl.gov and Stacey.Hill@inl.gov Responses must be received no later than: April 23, 2027 PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents should clearly identify any proprietary or confidential information contained within their submission. DISCLAIMER This Expression of Interest (EOI) is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or commitment by BEA or INL to procure supplies or services. BEA reserves the right to use information received through this EOI to evaluate market capabilities, acquisition strategies, and potential supplier interest. Submission of an EOI response does not guarantee participation in any future solicitation and does not obligate BEA or INL to award a contract. BEA is not responsible for any costs incurred by respondents in preparing or submitting responses to this EOI. Information obtained through this process may be used to assist in developing future procurement requirements and solicitation strategies
